rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says this phrase is explained in his Kitāb Taʾwīl al-Mushkil.
rows.anchor: مبين في كتاب "تأويل المشكل"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athāra means a remnant of knowledge inherited from the ancients.
rows.anchor: بقية من علم تؤثر عن الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading is athara, a noun on the faʿla pattern; the first reading athāra follows faʿāla.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ: (أثرة) (3) ؛ اسم مبني على "فعلة" من ذلك. والأول على "فعالة".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers mean that resurrection after death will not happen.
rows.anchor: يريدون: البعث بعد الموت؛ أي لا يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The load-bearing ones are clouds carrying water.
rows.anchor: {فالحاملات وقرا} السحاب تحمل الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The running ones are ships moving easily through the water.
rows.anchor: أي السفن تجري في الماء جريا سهلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative gloss says they run maysara, meaning they are made subservient.
rows.anchor: ويقال: تجري ميسرة؛ أي مسخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waffā means that Abraham reached or accomplished the intended end.
rows.anchor: {وإبراهيم الذي وفى} أي بلغ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yujzāhu means that he is recompensed for it.
rows.anchor: {ثم يجزاه} يجزى به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later creation is the second creation for resurrection on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: أي الخلق الثاني للبعث يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship sailed under God's sight and protection.
rows.anchor: أي بمرأى منا وحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people for whom the flood was retribution were Noah and the believers he carried with him.
rows.anchor: يعني: نوحا -عليه السلام- ومن حمله معه من المؤمنين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufira means that what Noah brought was denied.
rows.anchor: و (كفر) : جحد ما جاء به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudhdakir means someone who reflects and takes admonition.
rows.anchor: أي معتبر ومتعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudhdakir derives from iftiʿāl of dhikr: mudhtakir assimilated dhāl into tāʾ, then both letters became a doubled dāl.
rows.anchor: وأصله "مفتعل" من الذكر: "مذتكر". فأدغمت الذال في التاء ثم قلبتا دالا مشددة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nudhur is the plural of nadhīr, here meaning warning, so the phrase means punishment and warning; likewise nakīr means denial.
rows.anchor: جمع نذير. و "نذير" بمعنى الإنذار أي فكيف كان عذابي وإنذاري. ومثله: "النكير" بمعنى الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Quran easy to recite; otherwise people could neither articulate it nor listen to it.
rows.anchor: أي سهلناه للتلاوة. ولولا ذلك: ما أطاق العباد أن يلفظوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mudhāmmatān means intensely dark green from the richness of the greenery and moisture; Dhu al-Rumma's poetic word ḥabashiyya illustrates that deep green.
rows.anchor: قال ذو الرمة -وذكر غيثا-: كسا الأكم بهمى غضة حبشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tūrūn means that you extract fire from the firestrikers.
rows.anchor: {التي تورون} أي تستخرجون من الزنود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is a reminder that makes people remember Hell.
rows.anchor: {نحن جعلناها تذكرة} أي تذكركم جهنم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means benefit or use.
rows.anchor: {ومتاعا} أي منفعة (1) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muqwīn are travelers, named for lodging in al-qawāʾ, the empty desert.
rows.anchor: سموا بذلك: لنزولهم القواء وهو: القفر.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says al-muqwī is someone with no provisions, from aqwā al-rajul when his provisions run out.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: "المقوي: الذي لا زاد معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba prefers the traveler gloss and rejects Abu Ubayda's gloss: a person without provisions is not more in need of the fire than one with provisions; he says the latter is more in need.
rows.anchor: ولا أرى التفسير إلا الأول؛ ولا أرى الذي لا زاد معه أولى بالنار ولا أحوج إليها من الذي معه الزاد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night portioning passage, including half the night and increasing or decreasing it, is explained in Kitāb al-Mushkil.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {إلا قليلا * نصفه أو انقص منه قليلا * أو زد عليه} ؛ مفسر في كتاب "المشكل" (3) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says he has already discussed reciting the Quran with measured clarity in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl.
rows.anchor: {ورتل القرآن ترتيلا} قد ذكرناه في سورة بني إسرائيل (4) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabḥ means activity in one's needs, coming and going, and traveling back and forth.
rows.anchor: أي تصرفا في حوائجك، وإقبالا وإدبارا، [وذهابا ومجيئا]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattal ilayhi means devote yourself wholly to Him; it derives from battalt al-shayʾ, to cut it off.
rows.anchor: {وتبتل إليه} أي انقطع إليه. من قولك: بتلت الشيء؛ إذا قطعته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lan tuḥṣūhu means that you will not be able to manage or endure it.
rows.anchor: {علم أن لن تحصوه} لن تطيقوه (5) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man considered and plotted against Muhammad and his message, alternately calling him a poet, magician, or soothsayer, among similar accusations.
rows.anchor: في كيد محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وما جاء به، فقال: "شاعر" مرة، و "ساحر" مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means, What caused you to enter the Fire?
rows.anchor: {ما سلككم في سقر} ؟ أي ما أدخلكم النار؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkeys are frightened: they were alarmed and fled.
rows.anchor: {كأنهم حمر مستنفرة} مذعورة؛ استنفرت فنفرت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on the fāʾ, mustanfira means fleeing; an unnamed poet uses mustanfar for a fleeing donkey, supporting this sense.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ: (مستنفرة) بكسر الفاء (1) ؛ أراد: نافرة. قال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda identifies qaswara as a lion.
rows.anchor: {فرت من قسورة} قال أبو عبيدة: هو الأسد (3) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba connects qaswara tentatively to qasr, meaning overpowering, since a lion overpowers other beasts.
rows.anchor: وكأنه من "القسر" وهو: القهر. والأسد يقهر السباع.

rows.speaker: بعض التفسير
rows.claim: Some exegetical interpretation identifies qaswara as archers.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض التفسير: "أنهم الرماة" (4) .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's view that qaswara is the noise of people, meaning their sounds and voices.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن عيينة (5) . أن ابن عباس قال

rows.speaker: كفار قريش
rows.claim: Quraysh's unbelievers said that if a man's sin were recorded on a sheet, they could not understand why they did not see such a record themselves.
rows.anchor: قالت كفار قريش: "إن كان الرجل يذنب، فيكتب ذنبه في رقعة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is the Quran.
rows.anchor: {كلا إنه تذكرة} يعني: القرآن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nafs al-lawwāma is the soul that reproaches itself on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: (والنفس اللوامة) أي تلوم نفسها يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba refers readers to Kitāb Taʾwīl al-Mushkil for the explanation of this passage about gathering bones, shaping fingertips, and human persistence in sin.
rows.anchor: هذا مفسر في كتاب "تأويل المشكل" (3) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What reaches the collarbones is the soul, now situated between the person's collarbones.
rows.anchor: {كلا إذا بلغت التراقي} يعني: النفس؛ أي صارت النفس بين تراقيه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man rāq means, Is anyone there to perform healing or ruqya?
rows.anchor: {وقيل: من راق} ؟ أي هل أحد يرقي؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sudā means left neglected: neither commanded nor prohibited nor punished; asdaytu al-shayʾ means I left it neglected.
rows.anchor: {أن يترك سدى} أي يهمل: فلا يؤمر، ولا ينهى، ولا يعاقب (4) . يقال: أسديت الشيء؛ إذا أهملته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Matāʿ means benefit for you.
rows.anchor: {متاعا لكم} أي منفعة لكم (6) .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quddūs follows the faʿūl pattern and derives from quds, meaning purity.
rows.anchor: وهو حرف مبني على "فعول"؛ من "القدس" وهو: الطهارة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-arḍ al-muqaddasa means the land purified through blessing.
rows.anchor: "الأرض المقدسة" (3) ؛ يراد: المطهرة بالتبريك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the angels' statement, nuqaddisu laka means that they ascribe purity to God.
rows.anchor: {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} (4) ؛ أي: ننسبك إلى الطهارة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuqaddisuka and nuqaddisu laka, like nusabbihu laka and nusabbihuka, have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: و"نقدسك ونقدس لك" و"نسبح لك ونسبحك" بمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: أهل النظر
rows.claim: The people of speculation identify Ḥaẓīrat al-Quds as Paradise, a place purified from worldly impurities such as excrement, urine, and menstruation.
rows.anchor: حظيرة القدس - فيما قاله أهل النظر - هي: الجنة. لأنها موضع الطهارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrahs called al-miʾūn follow the seven long sūrahs; each has more than, or nearly, one hundred verses.
rows.anchor: و (السور التي تعرف بالمئين) هي ما ولي السبع الطوال، سميت بمئين لأن كل سور منها تزيد على مائة آية أو تقاربها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilḥād in God's names means deviating from the truth, including invoking al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and similar idols.
rows.anchor: والإلحاد (2) في أسمائه: [الجور عن الحق والعدول عنه، وذكر] اللات والعزى، وأشباه ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zabūr means something written, from zabara al-kitāb, to write it; its faʿūl pattern has passive meaning, like jalūb and rakūb for majlūb and markūb.
rows.anchor: و (الزبور) هو بمعنى مكتوب من زبر الكتاب يزبره إذا كتبه وهو فعول بمعنى مفعول، كما يقال: جلوب وركوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kataba al-kitāb means to gather its letters, as in katb al-kharaz, gathering beads in a row.
rows.anchor: أي جمع حروفه. ومنه كتب الخرز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Katabtu al-baghla describes joining the mare's two lips with a ring, another usage based on joining.
rows.anchor: ومنه يقال: كتبت البغلة: إذا جمعت بين شفريها بحلقة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatawaffā derives from istīfāʾ, taking something fully; tawaffaytuhu and istawfaytuhu, like other doubled forms, express this. Death was later called wafāt or waf.
rows.anchor: هو من استيفاء العدد واستيفاء الشيء إذا استقصيته كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs call blood nafs because it is connected to breath, following their practice of naming things for what is associated, adjacent, or causative.
rows.anchor: والعرب تسمى الدم نفسا لاتصال النفس به على مذهبهم في تسمية الشيء بما اتصل به أو جاوره أو كان سببا له

rows.speaker: أصحاب اللغة
rows.claim: The Arabs use nafisat al-marʾa for menstruation, as if she bled; lexicographers explain nafisāʾ as named for the flow of blood.
rows.anchor: ويقولون: نفست المرأة: إذا حاضت كأنها دميت. وقال أصحاب اللغة: وإنما سميت المرأة نفساء لسيلان الدم.

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrahim says anything without flowing blood does not render water impure if it falls into it; here nafs means flowing blood.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم (1) : كل شيء ليست له نفس سائلة فإنه لا ينجس الماء إذا سقط فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs also call the soul nasama, whose root is nafas.
rows.anchor: وتسمى العرب النفس نسمة. وأصل النسمة النفس.

rows.speaker: بعض الحديث
rows.claim: An unnamed hadith says to avoid dust because nasama comes from it; Ibn Qutayba explains nasama here as breath.
rows.anchor: وروي في بعض الحديث "تنكبوا الغبار فإن منه تكون النسمة" (2) يراد منه يكون النفس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabw is called nafs because it arises from breathing.
rows.anchor: والربو سمي نفسا لأنه عن النفس يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idioms ḥatfa nafsihi and ḥatfa anfihi mean dying in bed: breathing continues until death, when the soul leaves through the nose and mouth.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول: مات فلان حتف نفسه، وحتف أنفه إذا مات على فراشه؛
